Key Research Thinking Patterns: Multi-scale Thermal Downscaling and Validation: Bridging the resolution gap between coarse satellite observations and fine-scale urban features using machine learning regression to enhance the accuracy of local climate assessments (e.g., Random Forest downscaling of Landsat 8 LST to 10-m resolution using Sentinel-2 data).

Explainable AI-Driven Driver Analysis: Moving beyond black-box predictions by integrating SHapley Additive exPlanations with gradient boosting models to quantify the relative importance of morphological and environmental variables on thermal environments (e.g., XGBoost/SHAP analysis of urban heat island drivers).

Morphological Algorithmic Extraction: Applying advanced image processing and geometric logic to isolate individual biological entities from complex remote sensing imagery, enabling precise inventory and density estimation (e.g., Single Tree Extraction Method - Oil Palm using Gradient Difference Window Detection and Adaptive Iterative Erosion).

Efficiency Threshold Quantification: Establishing non-linear performance boundaries for ecological interventions to prevent resource overestimation and optimize planning efficacy (e.g., Threshold Value of Efficiency (TVoE) analysis of cooling effects in Beijing urban parks).

Landscape Ecology Metric Integration: Utilizing spatial pattern indices to correlate physical greenspace configuration with functional ecosystem services, guiding morphology-specific optimization strategies (e.g., Fragstats 4.2 calculation of Landscape Shape Index and Patch Cohesion for LCZ-specific planning).
Summary Description: Xiangming Xiao specializes in the intersection of urban climatology, tropical forestry, and geospatial intelligence. Leveraging high-resolution satellite imagery (Landsat, Sentinel, WorldView) and advanced machine learning (XGBoost, Random Forest), the researcher develops precise methods for urban heat island mitigation and single-tree extraction. Key contributions include downscaling thermal data for intra-urban analysis, applying Explainable AI to identify climate drivers, and quantifying efficiency thresholds for urban park cooling. This work bridges macro-level sustainable development goals with micro-scale ecological monitoring, providing robust, data-driven frameworks for climate-resilient urban planning and sustainable tropical resource management.
